EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretches at 2884 and 2918 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003, GFQ-039) and a CH2 scissoring band at 1454 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003), consistent with a saturated alkyl framework. Crucially, the set of bands at 1053, 1134, and 1155 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of multiple C–O stretching vibrations expected when both an alcohol (C–O(H)) and an ether (C–O–C) are present; candidate 1 uniquely contains both functionalities, explaining the two higher-frequency C–O bands near 1134–1155 along with the lower one near ~1053. The cluster of skeletal modes between 800–1000 cm⁻¹ fits aliphatic systems without carbonyl or aromatic features. Pure hydrocarbon (10) would not account for the 1134–1155 region, and single-function alcohols (3–7) less naturally explain multiple C–O stretch bands.
